name: Koutras-McIntosh Spacetimes
description: Null radiation in a conformally flat spacetime whose curvature scalars of every order are zero and which in general has no Killing vector and no homothety. Where the radiation is weak its fronts are half planes tangent to a cylinder growing at the speed of light, and concentrated on one front it is an impulsive pp-wave.
convention: The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Pure radiation is energy streaming at the speed of light along a single null direction, with a stress tensor proportional to $l_a l_b$ for a null vector $l$ [edgarludwig1997]. Dietrich Kramer, Hans Stephani, Malcolm MacCallum, and Eduard Herlt concluded in their book of exact solutions that every conformally flat spacetime filled with pure radiation is a plane wave [edgarludwig1997ghp]. Patrick Wils found one in 1989 that is not, and pointed out that it contradicts their Theorem 32.17 [wils1989, edgarludwig1997]. Wils took the metric to complete the class of conformally flat fields of pure radiation that are not plane waves [edgarludwig1997ghp]. Its Weyl tensor vanishes, one free function $f(u)$ of a null coordinate $u$ sets the strength of the radiation, and spacetime is flat where $f$ vanishes [edgarludwig1997, griffithspodolsky1998].¶Relativists decide whether two metrics describe one spacetime by comparing the components of the Riemann tensor and of its covariant derivatives in frames fixed by the curvature, one order of derivative at a time, until an order brings nothing new [koutras1992, edgarvickers1999]. Relativists had expected no spacetime to need more than the third order [koutras1992]. Andreas Koutras showed in 1992 that Wils's metric needs the fourth, the first spacetime known to do so [koutras1992, edgarvickers1999]. Koutras found as well that the metric admits at most one Killing vector and one homothety, and in general no Killing vector [koutras1992, edgarludwig1997ghp].¶Koutras and Colin McIntosh rewrote Wils's metric in 1996 and gave a family with two constants $a$ and $b$, $$ds^2 = \left(a^2w^2 - 2f(u)\,(ax + b)(x^2 + y^2)\right)du^2 - 2(ax + b)\,du\,dw + 2aw\,du\,dx + dx^2 + dy^2,$$ which is a plane wave at $a = 0$ and Wils's metric at $b = 0$ [koutrasmcintosh1996, edgarludwig1997, griffithspodolsky1998]. They called it "A metric with no symmetries or invariants" [koutrasmcintosh1996]. Every scalar built from its Riemann tensor and from the covariant derivatives of that tensor vanishes, as each one does in flat space, and for general $a$, $b$, and $f$ it admits no isometry and no homothety, even locally [koutrasmcintosh1996]. In a null frame its curvature has one nonzero component, the Ricci component of the radiation, $\Phi_{22} = 2f(u)/(ax + b)$ [griffithspodolsky1998].¶S. Brian Edgar and Garry Ludwig set out to derive Wils's metric again, to test a method of integration that rests on four independent scalars of the geometry, which a spacetime with no Killing vector supplies [edgarludwig1997ghp]. They obtained in 1997 the whole class of conformally flat spacetimes of pure radiation that are not plane waves, with three free functions $f(u)$, $g(u)$, and $h(u)$; it contains Koutras and McIntosh's family with $a \neq 0$ and reduces to Wils's metric when $g$ and $h$ vanish [edgarludwig1997, edgarludwig1997ghp]. The rays of every such spacetime neither expand, shear, nor twist, so it belongs to Wolfgang Kundt's class, and no null electromagnetic field, massless scalar field, or neutrino field can be its source [edgarludwig1997, griffithspodolsky1998]. Jim Skea classified the class with the program CLASSI and found that it is wider than Wils's metric and that none of its members needs more than the fourth order [edgarludwig1997, skea1997]. The functions $g$ and $h$ first appear in the second derivatives of the curvature, and telling Wils's metric from the rest takes the fourth [griffithspodolsky1998].¶Jerry Griffiths and Jiří Podolský took the source to be a null fluid of incoherent radiation and interpreted its geometry in 1998 [griffithspodolsky1998]. Where the radiation is weak, its wave surfaces are half planes tangent to a cylinder whose radius grows at the speed of light, each one turned about the cylinder's axis from the one before, for Wils's metric and the whole class alike [griffithspodolsky1998]. An observer outside sees the radiation arrive from a direction that turns until the edge of the cylinder passes, coming last along the radius [griffithspodolsky1998]. Concentrated on one front, the radiation is an impulsive pp-wave whose direction of travel depends on the front [griffithspodolsky1998]. The cylinder, at $x = 0$, is the envelope of the fronts, and Griffiths and Podolský took it for a coordinate singularity with a void of flat space inside [griffithspodolsky1998]. Podolský and Miroslav Beláň followed null geodesics toward it in 2004 and found components of the curvature in a parallelly propagated frame diverging there, so the cylinder is a curvature singularity at which every curvature scalar vanishes [podolskybelan2004].¶Alan Barnes solved the conformal Killing equations of the class in 2001 and found fifteen conformal symmetries, as conformal flatness requires, and in general no Killing vector and no homothety [barnes2001]. Wils's metric with constant $f$ has both, which together make a group of homotheties of two dimensions that Ludwig and Edgar had missed [barnes2001]. Podolský and Ondřej Prikryl wrote the class and its extensions to a cosmological constant in one system of coordinates in 2009 and confirmed the derivations made with invariant operators [podolskyprikryl2009]. Boris Kruglikov and Wijnand Steneker, writing of the Koutras-McIntosh spacetimes in 2022, proved that they have Killing vectors only when $a = 0$, the plane waves, or when $b = 0$ and $f(u) = (c_0 + c_1u + c_2u^2)^{-2}$ [kruglikovsteneker2022]. For generic $a$, $b$, and $f$ they found no Killing tensor up to degree six beyond the energy and its powers, which are then the only conserved quantities of a free particle polynomial in its momentum up to that degree [kruglikovsteneker2022].

related.text: The family at $a = 0$ and $b = 1$, a plane wave of pure radiation whose profile is quadratic and the same in every direction across it, so that its Weyl tensor vanishes [griffithspodolsky1998, kruglikovsteneker2022].

The gravitational waves of Kundt's class, whose rays neither expand nor twist. Where they are weak their fronts are the same half planes tangent to a cylinder growing at the speed of light, and the cylinder is a curvature singularity in both [griffithspodolsky1998, podolskybelan2004].

Waves crossing anti-de Sitter space. With a negative cosmological constant, part of the conformally flat class of pure radiation is the conformally flat subfamily of Siklos's waves [podolskyprikryl2009].
The radiation turned off. At $f = 0$ the metric is flat space, in coordinates that end on a cylinder growing at the speed of light [griffithspodolsky1998].

coordinates.name: Koutras-McIntosh
domains: ax + b > 0 \;\text{(the side of the envelope the radiation fills)}
ax + b = 0 \;\text{(the envelope of the wave fronts, for } a \neq 0\text{)}

parameters.description: A pure number. With $a = 0$ and $b > 0$ the metric is a plane wave, and with $b = 0$ it is Wils's metric
A length; for $a \neq 0$ the envelope of the wave fronts is $ax + b = 0$
Amplitude of the radiation, an inverse length, a function of $u$ alone; the Ricci tensor is $R_{uu} = 4(ax + b)f$, and $f = 0$ is flat space

coordinates.convention: We use Koutras and McIntosh's coordinates $(u, w, x, y)$, with $u$ a pure number labelling the wave fronts, $w$ a length along the rays, and $x$ and $y$ lengths on the front. We leave the amplitude $f$ free. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = dx^2 + dy^2 - 2\left(ax + b\right)du\,dw + 2aw\,du\,dx + \left(a^2w^2 - 2f\left(ax + b\right)\left(x^2 + y^2\right)\right)du^2

nonzero.value: \dfrac{\left(a\,x + b\right)\left(x^2 + y^2\right)\partial_u f + a\,f\,w\left(a\,x^2 - a\,y^2 + 2b\,x\right)}{a\,x + b}

geodesics: \ddot{w} + \dfrac{\left(a\,x + b\right)\left(x^2 + y^2\right)\partial_u f + a\,f\,w\left(a\,x^2 - a\,y^2 + 2b\,x\right)}{a\,x + b}\dot{u}^2 + \dfrac{2f\left(a\,x^2 - a\,y^2 + 2b\,x\right)}{a\,x + b}\dot{u}\dot{x} + 4f\,y\,\dot{u}\dot{y} = 0

coordinates.name: Edgar-Ludwig
domains: x = 0 \;\text{(the envelope of the wave fronts)}

parameters.description: Amplitude of the radiation, an inverse length, a function of $u$ alone; the Ricci tensor is $R_{uu} = 4xf$, and $f = 0$ is flat space
A length, a function of $u$ alone, absent from the Ricci tensor; with $g = h = 0$ the metric is Wils's
An area, a function of $u$ alone, absent from the Ricci tensor; with $g$ and $h$ constant the metric is Wils's in other coordinates

coordinates.convention: We use Wils's coordinates $(u, v, x, y)$, with $u$ a pure number labelling the wave fronts, $v$ an area along the rays, and $x$ and $y$ lengths on the front; $v = xw$ in Koutras and McIntosh's coordinates at $a = 1$ and $b = 0$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = dx^2 + dy^2 - 2\,du\,dv + \dfrac{4v}{x}du\,dx + \left(\dfrac{v^2}{x^2} - 2fx\left(x^2 + y^2 + gy + h\right)\right)du^2

nonzero.value: \dfrac{x^5\left(x^2 + y^2 + g\,y + h\right)\partial_u f + f\,x^5\left(4v + y\,\partial_u g + \partial_u h\right) - v^3}{x^4}
-x\left(\left(x^2 + y^2 + g\,y + h\right)\partial_u f + f\left(y\,\partial_u g + \partial_u h\right)\right)

geodesics: \ddot{v} + \dfrac{x^5\left(x^2 + y^2 + g\,y + h\right)\partial_u f + f\,x^5\left(4v + y\,\partial_u g + \partial_u h\right) - v^3}{x^4}\dot{u}^2 + \dfrac{2v}{x^2}\dot{u}\dot{v} + \dfrac{2f\,x^3\left(x^2 - y^2 - g\,y - h\right) - 4v^2}{x^3}\dot{u}\dot{x} + 2f\,x\left(2y + g\right)\dot{u}\dot{y} - \dfrac{2}{x}\dot{v}\dot{x} + \dfrac{2v}{x^2}\dot{x}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Kerr-Schild
domains: X^2 + Z^2 > c^2T^2 \;\text{(outside the envelope of the wave fronts)}
cT + Z = 0,\; X < 0 \;\text{(the wave front } u \to \pm\infty\text{)}

parameters.description: A length setting the strength of the radiation, $f = 1/\ell$, positive so that the energy density is positive
Distance along a wave front from the line where it touches the envelope, the cylinder $X^2 + Z^2 = c^2T^2$
Label of the wave front through the event, $u = \tan(\alpha/2)$ for the front $cT = X\sin\alpha + Z\cos\alpha$
A coordinate along the rays; $2xv = cT + Z$ is the $w$ of Koutras and McIntosh's chart at $a = 1$ and $b = 0$

coordinates.convention: We use the inertial coordinates $(T, X, Y, Z)$ of the flat space the radiation crosses, with $T$ a time, for Wils's metric with $f = 1/\ell$; $x$, $u$, and $v$ are the coordinates of the Kundt form as functions of these. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cT$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{T}$ means $d(cT)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -c^2dT^2 + dX^2 + dY^2 + dZ^2 - \dfrac{x^2 + Y^2}{2\ell x}\left(\left(1 + u^2\right)c\,dT - 2u\,dX - \left(1 - u^2\right)dZ\right)^2
geodesics: \ddot{T} - \dfrac{\left(u^2 + 1\right)^2\left(u^2\,v\,x^2 - u^2\,v\,Y^2 - u\,x^2 - 3u\,Y^2 + v\,x^2 - v\,Y^2\right)}{4x^2\,\ell}\dot{T}^2 + \dfrac{\left(u^2 + 1\right)\left(2u^3\,v\,x^2 - 2u^3\,v\,Y^2 - 3u^2\,x^2 - 5u^2\,Y^2 + 2u\,v\,x^2 - 2u\,v\,Y^2 + x^2 - Y^2\right)}{2x^2\,\ell}\dot{T}\dot{X} + \dfrac{Y\left(u^2 + 1\right)^2}{x\,\ell}\dot{T}\dot{Y} - \dfrac{\left(u^2 + 1\right)\left(u^4\,v\,x^2 - u^4\,v\,Y^2 - u^3\,x^2 - 3u^3\,Y^2 + 3u\,x^2 + u\,Y^2 - v\,x^2 + v\,Y^2\right)}{2x^2\,\ell}\dot{T}\dot{Z} - \dfrac{u\left(u^3\,v\,x^2 - u^3\,v\,Y^2 - 2u^2\,x^2 - 2u^2\,Y^2 + u\,v\,x^2 - u\,v\,Y^2 + x^2 - Y^2\right)}{x^2\,\ell}\dot{X}^2 - \dfrac{2u\,Y\left(u^2 + 1\right)}{x\,\ell}\dot{X}\dot{Y} + \dfrac{2u^5\,v\,x^2 - 2u^5\,v\,Y^2 - 3u^4\,x^2 - 5u^4\,Y^2 + 8u^2\,x^2 - 2u\,v\,x^2 + 2u\,v\,Y^2 - x^2 + Y^2}{2x^2\,\ell}\dot{X}\dot{Z} + \dfrac{Y\left(u^2 + 1\right)\left(u^2 - 1\right)}{x\,\ell}\dot{Y}\dot{Z} - \dfrac{\left(u^2 - 1\right)\left(u^4\,v\,x^2 - u^4\,v\,Y^2 - u^3\,x^2 - 3u^3\,Y^2 + 5u\,x^2 - u\,Y^2 - v\,x^2 + v\,Y^2\right)}{4x^2\,\ell}\dot{Z}^2 = 0

\ddot{Z} + \dfrac{\left(u^2 + 1\right)\left(u^4\,v\,x^2 - u^4\,v\,Y^2 - u^3\,x^2 - 3u^3\,Y^2 - 5u\,x^2 + u\,Y^2 - v\,x^2 + v\,Y^2\right)}{4x^2\,\ell}\dot{T}^2 - \dfrac{2u^5\,v\,x^2 - 2u^5\,v\,Y^2 - 3u^4\,x^2 - 5u^4\,Y^2 - 8u^2\,x^2 - 2u\,v\,x^2 + 2u\,v\,Y^2 - x^2 + Y^2}{2x^2\,\ell}\dot{T}\dot{X} - \dfrac{Y\left(u^2 + 1\right)\left(u^2 - 1\right)}{x\,\ell}\dot{T}\dot{Y} + \dfrac{\left(u^2 - 1\right)\left(u^4\,v\,x^2 - u^4\,v\,Y^2 - u^3\,x^2 - 3u^3\,Y^2 - 3u\,x^2 - u\,Y^2 - v\,x^2 + v\,Y^2\right)}{2x^2\,\ell}\dot{T}\dot{Z} + \dfrac{u\left(u^3\,v\,x^2 - u^3\,v\,Y^2 - 2u^2\,x^2 - 2u^2\,Y^2 - u\,v\,x^2 + u\,v\,Y^2 - x^2 + Y^2\right)}{x^2\,\ell}\dot{X}^2 + \dfrac{2u\,Y\left(u^2 - 1\right)}{x\,\ell}\dot{X}\dot{Y} - \dfrac{\left(u^2 - 1\right)\left(2u^3\,v\,x^2 - 2u^3\,v\,Y^2 - 3u^2\,x^2 - 5u^2\,Y^2 - 2u\,v\,x^2 + 2u\,v\,Y^2 - x^2 + Y^2\right)}{2x^2\,\ell}\dot{X}\dot{Z} - \dfrac{Y\left(u^2 - 1\right)^2}{x\,\ell}\dot{Y}\dot{Z} + \dfrac{\left(u^2 - 1\right)^2\left(u^2\,v\,x^2 - u^2\,v\,Y^2 - u\,x^2 - 3u\,Y^2 - v\,x^2 + v\,Y^2\right)}{4x^2\,\ell}\dot{Z}^2 = 0
